summary: This document describes an RDAP extension for how responses are redacted, and for marking which fields are redacted. It uses JSONPath as the default expression language to point at redacted fields.

eli5.summary: When some words are blacked out in a document, a note should say which. This tells RDAP responses to mark exactly what was hidden.

questions: how does rdap mark redacted fields
what is the redacted member in rdap
subtitle: How an RDAP server tells you which fields it hid, and how, instead of leaving you guessing.

tldr.problem: An RDAP response can leave out a field because the data does not exist or because the client lacks privilege to see it, and the client cannot tell which.
tldr.mechanism: A redacted response carries a redacted member listing each affected field, a name, a JSONPath to it, and one of four methods: removal, emptyValue, partialValue or replacementValue.
tldr.outcome: Clients can tell redaction apart from other reasons for missing data. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 9537 is a Proposed Standard (Standards Track) published in March 2024, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It uses the JSONPath language of RFC 9535 and is companion reading to RFC 9536.

sections.title: What Redaction Means in RDAP
sections.content:
A redacted RDAP field is one that has data removed or replaced in the response because of server policy, such as the client lacking privilege to receive it. This extension can flag redacted fields in any RDAP object class from RFC 9083, or in fields defined by RDAP extensions.

The point is disambiguation. A field may be missing because there is no data or because the client may not see it. By listing redacted fields explicitly, the server lets the client tell the two apart. It applies to a single object in a lookup response and to each object in a search response (RFC 9082).

JSONPath (RFC 9535) is the default language for pointing at the redacted fields.
sections.eli5: If a page in a book is missing, you want to know whether it was torn out or never printed. This lets the server say it was hidden on purpose.

sections.title: The Four Redaction Methods
sections.content:
The redacted response MUST still follow the RDAP formats. Placeholder text such as XXXX MUST NOT be used as redaction, because it may not fit the format of each field and would be an inconsistent signal. The methods exist because RDAP mixes JSON objects with JSON arrays, notably in jCard, where position in the array carries meaning.

  • Removal (the default): the field is deleted. Removing an object removes its children, and only the object needs to be listed. It MUST NOT be used on an array element whose position carries meaning, because that would break the jCard.
  • Empty value: the value is set to "" for text or null for non-text. It MUST be used only for fields identified by array position. The required fn property MUST use it, since removing the property or its value would violate vCard or jCard.
  • Partial value: part of the data is removed, as with the label or fn properties. It SHOULD be used only for formatted values.
  • Replacement value: the value is replaced, for example with an anonymized email text value, or with a contact-uri property pointing to a web form.
sections.eli5: You can cut a word out, leave a blank, black out half of it, or write a different word in its place. Each way gets its own name.

sections.title: The redacted Member
sections.content:
The redacted member MUST be added when one or more fields are redacted. It sits on the object in a lookup response and on each object in a search response. Responses that use it MUST include redacted in rdapConformance. A server MAY leave out entries for fields where even a signal that data exists would be a privacy issue, and MAY publish a redaction policy.

The member holds an array of objects with these children:

  • name (REQUIRED): a logical name, given as a registered type or an unregistered description.
  • prePath: JSON path in the response before redaction. For removal and replacement. MUST NOT be set with postPath.
  • postPath: JSON path in the redacted response. MUST be set for empty value and partial value, and for replacement when the field remains.
  • replacementPath: path to the replacement field.
  • pathLang: path language, default jsonpath.
  • method: removal (the default), emptyValue, partialValue or replacementValue.
  • reason: human-readable reason. Its description MUST NOT be a client processing dependency.
sections.eli5: It is a list of notes. Each note names the hidden thing, says where it was, how it was hidden and, if the server wants, why.

sections.title: A Redacted Lookup Response
sections.content:
The RFC shows a domain lookup for example.com before and after redaction. Among other changes, the registry domain ID handle is removed, the registrant fn is set to an empty string, the registrant organization and email are removed, and the administrative and billing contacts are removed entirely with reasons that point to the technical and registrant contacts.

For a search response, each domain in domainSearchResults carries its own redacted array, with paths such as $.domainSearchResults[0].handle.

The JSONPath expressions in the examples are for illustration with single-role entities. The exact expressions a server uses are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Imagine a class list where one child's name is blanked and another child's whole row is cut out. A note at the bottom lists each change.

sections.title: JSONPath Guidance
sections.content:
For clients, the main point is that with removal, or with replacement by an alternative field, the prePath will not resolve in the redacted response. The client can key off the name member for display logic.

For servers, the RFC lists considerations:

  • Use absolute paths starting with $, such as $.handle.
  • Check prePath expressions against the non-redacted response, where they should return the redacted field.
  • When removing an object, reference the object itself.
  • If several policies apply, a server must include at least one entry but should consider one entry per basis for redaction.
  • For jCard removal, reference the property with a filter on index 0, the property name.
  • For jCard empty value, reference values at array index 3 and greater, for example the postal code.

RDAP extensions should define any special JSONPath considerations they need.
sections.eli5: The server gives exact directions to each spot. If something was cut out, the directions lead nowhere, so the label tells you what it was.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the extension identifier redacted in the 'RDAP Extensions' registry. It also extended the 'RDAP JSON Values' registry from RFC 9083 with three new Type values: redacted name, redacted reason and redacted expression language. The value jsonpath was registered as a redacted expression language, pointing to RFC 9535.
sections.eli5: There is an official list of names and reasons servers can use, so different servers say the same thing the same way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extension does not provide any security services beyond those described by RFC 9083. The one point the RFC raises elsewhere is that a redacted signal tells an unauthorized client that data exists, which is why a server MAY omit entries for sensitive fields.
sections.eli5: Saying that something was hidden can itself give a clue. So a server may choose to say nothing about the most sensitive items.

items.desc: Value set to an empty string or null; for array-position fields.

items.label: Redaction by Partial Value
items.desc: Part of a formatted value removed.
